arguments.goal: mac2mac: a CLI that lets one Mac dispatch a task to another Mac via Claude Agent SDK and stream the result back. v0 = one-way (controller → worker), Tailscale + WebSocket + bearer token, Python SDK, receiver-side permissions scope tool use.
arguments.metric: First end-to-end round-trip: `mac2mac --target=worker "echo hello && pwd"` from Mac A returns Mac B's pwd output, with bearer-token auth enforced and no Tailscale-bypass path. Then: same call survives a 24h soak (worker daemon stays up, reconnects after sleep).

warnings.detail: Goal has no matching entry in this repo's `.research-md/`, `.visionlog/`, or `.lighthouse/`. Consequential work should be earned via research.md and recorded as an ADR in visionlog before execution begins. If this goal is small/obvious, ignore. If it spawns substantial work, pause and go upstream.

arguments.action_summary: Wrote full protocol spec in docs/SPEC.md (sections: arch, discovery, pairing, transport, wire protocol, conversation lifecycle with state machine, agent tools, permissions, logging, failure modes, deferred work). Wrote README.md as user-facing entry. Updated AUTONOMY.md with conversation termination decisions. Added explicit design for the bye-bye case: end envelopes are structural and never become user-turns on the receiving side, so A does not auto-respond to B's reciprocal end.

Iteration 2: ran cept audit on v0 spec. Added 6 worked-example transcripts (§11), token rotation procedure (§3.4), threat model with 7-adversary table (§8.4), three new safety mechanisms to §6.2 (LLM token budget, rate limit, agent response timeout — bringing total to 5), `ack.reason` enum field. Resolved 4 of 5 prior open questions; added 3 new ones. Cept's design verdict: structural end_conversation is sane prior art (conf 0.9), daemon-level runaway prevention is sufficient (conf 0.85). Cept's counter-recommendation was "stop researching, start coding" — noted but user directive is docs-only.
arguments.measurement: spec_sections=14, worked_examples=6, safety_mechanisms=5, threat_model_adversaries=7, open_questions_resolved=4_of_5, new_open_questions=3, code=0_lines

arguments.action_summary: Iteration 3: wrote docs/BUILD-PLAN.md collapsing the spec to a single v0.1 acceptance test (hostname round-trip + structural bye-bye). Defined a file-by-file dep graph, 6 phased build steps with named exit criteria, test strategy across unit/single-Mac/two-Mac, 5-row risk register, stop conditions, and a definition-of-done checklist. Resolved 2 more open questions (Q7 multi-agent envelope future-proofing = yes; Q8 reconnect resume = closed on disconnect for v0.1). Added Q9 (token budget default = defer until soak data). Net effect: every blocking decision for starting v0.1 implementation is now locked.

Iteration 4: PIVOTED FROM DESIGN TO BUILD per user feedback (spec-hypertrophy diagnosis). Wrote first working code: pyproject.toml + 5 src files (protocol/transport/daemon/cli/__main__) implementing the simplest cross-process envelope round-trip. Verified: 'mac2mac serve' + 'mac2mac say hello from cli' returns 'you said: hello from cli'. Skipped pairing/keychain/identity/Tailscale/WS — that's later Phases. This proves the protocol shape locally before adding the network layer. Phase gate in AUTONOMY.md honored: this iteration produced code, not docs.
